newsitem.title: UK: Cathay urges annual cargo rate adjustments.
newsitem.headline: Cathay urges annual cargo rate adjustments.

text.p: Cathay Pacific Airways,, with the support of the British Shippers' Council (BSC), has urged airlines to "adjust" their cargo rates for forwarders and shippers annually instead of the twice-yearly policy adopted by most carriers.

"For the past two years, we have imposed just one cargo rate rise a year on our top six UK agents, which are responsible for providing more than 60 percent of our business, because they asked for it," said Cathay's UK and Ireland cargo manager Mark Olney.
"It has worked well for us. Quite clearly, most businesses budget their costs a year in advance and it is silly for airlines not adjust their tariffs accordingly on a once-yearly basis," he added.
Andrew Traill, the BSC's shipping and air manager, said by adjusting rates annually instead of twice-yearly, airlines would also benefit.
"They would be better able to plan ahead for expected demand. By adjusting rates just once a year, seasonal rate fluctuations which now happen could come to an end," he said.
Olney said he was willing to consider extending his annual rate rise policy to cover dealings with all of Cathay's forwarder and shipper customers in Britain.
"We could well do this if it suits us. It would certainly mean less work for us," he said.

The cargo departments of airlines have traditionally "adjusted" -- airfreight industry terminology for increased -- their rates at the start of new spring and autumn timetable schedules. -Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 -www.racs.com
